mainTopic: Becoming טמא in the עזרה, the dispute over forgetting the מקדש, how to count the ידיעות, and two unresolved questions about partial knowledge.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the משנה. An addition to the עזרה made without the full ceremony does not make a טמא person liable for entering it. A person who became טמא inside the עזרה and forgot one fact or both brings a קרבן עולה ויורד if he bowed, stayed as long as a bow takes, or left by the long way. If he left by the short way, he is פטור. The משנה ties this to הוריות and contrasts it with the מצוה of נדה, where pulling out immediately makes a man חייב. רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא hold there is no קרבן for forgetting the מקדש, and רבי ישמעאל holds there is. In the גמרא, רב פפא and אביי debate how 'two that are four' adds up. The two versions of רב פפא's answer disagree about which four of the eight kinds of knowing the תנא counts. Two questions about partial knowledge, a lentil-sized שרץ and a newcomer who does not know where the מקדש is, both end in תיקו. Finally, רב שימי בר חייא begins bringing a פסוק as the source that additions to the עזרה are treated like the original, and the quote continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the expansion ceremony, and when entering the new area counts
steps.stepSummary: At the end of the ceremony the inner תודה is eaten and the outer one is burned. An addition made without the full ceremony does not make a טמא person liable for entering it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The inner thanks-offering is eaten and the outer one is burned. Any addition that was not made with all these procedures: one who enters there is not liable for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes describing the ceremony for adding to ירושלים or the עזרה. It then rules that an addition made without this full ceremony does not make a טמא person liable for entering it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new area becomes holy only through the complete ceremony: מלך, נביא, אורים ותומים, סנהדרין, two תודות, and singing. If any part is missing, the area does not get the קדושה of the מקדש. So a טמא person who enters it is not liable for a קרבן or for כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: The inner one (of the two תודה offerings in the procession)
The outer one
Is burned
With all these (the full list of ceremony requirements)

steps.whatToRemember: Adding to the מקדש area requires the full ceremony. Without it, the new area does not carry the חיוב for a טמא person who enters.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the boundary for everything that follows. The laws of טומאת מקדש apply only to places that truly have the קדושה of the מקדש.

phrases.english: the inner one is eaten,
phrases.notes: This is talking about the two תודה offerings carried in the procession when the area is being expanded.

phrases.english: and the outer one is burned.
And any [addition] that was not made with all these,
one who enters there is not liable for it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה's description of the expansion ceremony, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An addition to the מקדש made without the full ceremony does not obligate a טמא person who enters it.

steps.title: Becoming impure while already inside the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: Someone who became טמא inside the עזרה and forgot either fact, or both, is חייב if he bowed, stayed as long as a bow takes, or left by the long way. If he left by the short way, he is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he became impure in the courtyard, and the impurity was hidden from him but he remembered the Temple, or the Temple was hidden from him but he remembered the impurity, or both were hidden from him, and he bowed, or stayed long enough to bow, or left by the long way, he is liable. By the short way, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה switches to a new case: a person who was טהור when he entered and became טמא while inside the עזרה. It tells us when he must bring a קרבן and when he does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This person did nothing wrong by entering, so the only question is how he leaves. Staying long enough to bow, or taking the longer route, counts as remaining in the מקדש while טמא, so he is חייב. Leaving by the shortest route is exactly what the Torah requires of him, so he is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: The Temple courtyard
Was hidden from him (he forgot)
Stayed as long as it takes to bow
By the long route
By the short route

steps.confusionAlert: 'Hidden from him' is the reason a קרבן applies at all. A קרבן is for doing something by mistake. If he knew both facts and stayed on purpose, this would no longer be a case for a קרבן.

phrases.english: If he became impure in the courtyard,

phrases.aramaic: וְנֶעֶלְמָה מִמֶּנּוּ טוּמְאָה וְזָכוּר אֶת הַמִּקְדָּשׁ;
phrases.english: and the impurity was hidden from him but he remembers the Temple;
or the Temple was hidden from him but he remembers the impurity;
or both this and that were hidden from him;
and he bowed, or he stayed long enough to bow,
or he went out by the long way, he is liable.
By the short way, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the case of someone who entered while טמא to someone who became טמא while already inside.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person who became טמא in the עזרה is חייב a קרבן if he bowed, stayed as long as a bow takes, or left by the long route. He is פטור if he left by the shortest route.

steps.title: This is the Temple מצוה for which there is no liability
steps.stepSummary: The משנה identifies this rule, that a טמא person must leave the מקדש, as the מצות עשה of the מקדש for which בית דין is not liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the positive מצוה concerning the Temple for which one is not liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה labels the case it just taught. It is the 'מצות עשה of the מקדש' mentioned in another משנה, the one for which there is no liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה in הוריות speaks of a מצות עשה of the מקדש for which בית דין does not bring a פר if they rule wrongly. Our משנה explains which מצוה that is: leaving the מקדש by the short way after becoming טמא. The reason is that this sin carries a קרבן עולה ויורד, not a fixed חטאת, and בית דין brings a פר only for a sin that carries a fixed חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive commandment (a 'do' מצוה)
One is not liable for it (here: בית דין does not bring a פר for ruling wrongly about it)

steps.whyThisMatters: It links this case to the rules of הוריות. It shows that a sin carrying a קרבן עולה ויורד is treated differently from one carrying a fixed חטאת.

phrases.english: This is the positive מצוה concerning the Temple
phrases.notes: A משנה in הוריות mentions a Temple מצוה, and our משנה is telling you which one it means.

phrases.english: for which one is not liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the rule from the previous step as the 'מצות עשה of the מקדש' mentioned elsewhere.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מצוה for a טמא person to leave the מקדש is the מצות עשה of the מקדש for which בית דין is not liable.

steps.title: Which מצוה of נדה does carry liability?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks what the matching מצות עשה of נדה is, for which there is liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: And which is the positive מצוה with regard to a menstruating woman for which one is liable?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks a question to set up its next point. It wants to identify the מצות עשה of נדה that the same משנה in הוריות mentions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in הוריות contrasts two מצוות: one of the מקדש with no liability and one of נדה with liability. Having explained the first, our משנה now asks which מצוה the second one is. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A menstruating woman
And which is it?
For which one is liable

phrases.english: And which is the positive מצוה concerning a menstruating woman
for which one is liable?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁבַּנִּדָּה שֶׁחַיָּיבִין עָלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the מקדש half of the pair to the נדה half.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which מצות עשה regarding נדה carries liability, as mentioned in הוריות?

steps.title: Pulling out right away still counts as a sin
steps.stepSummary: If a woman becomes טמאה during relations and the man pulls out immediately, he is חייב, because pulling out gives him pleasure just like entering.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was having relations with a pure woman and she said to him 'I have become impure,' and he withdrew immediately, he is liable, because his withdrawal is as pleasurable to him as his entry.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its question. The מצות עשה of נדה is how a man must separate when his wife becomes טמאה during relations. Pulling out immediately makes him חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might expect that pulling out right away is the right thing to do. The משנה teaches that pulling out gives him pleasure just like entering, so it counts as an act of relations with a נדה. This sin carries a fixed חטאת, so בית דין is liable for a wrong ruling about it, unlike the מקדש case.

keyTerms.meaning: Having marital relations
I have become impure
He withdrew immediately
His withdrawal
Like his entry

steps.whatToRemember: The two halves of the pair: in the מקדש, the right way to leave (the short way) means no liability. With נדה, pulling out immediately is itself a sin with a fixed חטאת, so בית דין can be liable for ruling wrongly about it.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume 'he left immediately' means he did the right thing. The משנה says this immediate withdrawal is exactly what makes him חייב.

phrases.english: If he was having relations with a pure woman
and she said to him: 'I have become impure,'
and he withdrew immediately, he is liable,
because his withdrawal is as pleasurable to him as his entry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case of a man who pulls out immediately when his wife says she became טמאה. He is חייב because withdrawing gives pleasure like entering.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: Liable only for forgetting the שרץ
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר reads the פסוק to say a person is liable for forgetting the טומאה of the שרץ, but not for forgetting the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: The פסוק says 'the שרץ' and then 'and it is hidden from him.' So if he forgot about the שרץ, he is liable. If he forgot about the מקדש, he is not liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings רבי אליעזר's opinion on which kind of forgetting obligates a person to bring a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, the words 'and it is hidden from him' come right after the word 'שרץ'. רבי אליעזר learns from this that the thing that was hidden is the שרץ, meaning the טומאה itself. So forgetting the מקדש does not bring a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: A small creeping creature whose dead body makes a person טמא
A lapse of awareness, something being forgotten or hidden from a person
'And it is hidden from him', words from the פסוק
Liable, here meaning obligated to bring a קרבן

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
"The creeping animal", "and it is hidden from him"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:2. The two phrases sit next to each other in the פסוק, and that is his whole point.

phrases.english: for forgetting the creeping animal, he is liable,
but he is not liable for forgetting the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic in the משנה: the source for which kind of forgetting brings a קרבן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability comes only for forgetting the טומאה, which is learned from the closeness of 'השרץ' and 'ונעלם ממנו'. There is no liability for forgetting the מקדש.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: Liable only for forgetting the טומאה
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא reaches the same ruling as רבי אליעזר from a different phrase: 'and it is hidden from him, and he is טמא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: The פסוק says 'and it is hidden from him, and he is טמא.' So if he forgot that he was טמא, he is liable. If he forgot the מקדש, he is not liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא agrees with רבי אליעזר's ruling but learns it from different words in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא connects 'it is hidden from him' to the words 'and he is טמא'. That shows the thing hidden is his טומאה. Like רבי אליעזר, he holds there is no קרבן for forgetting the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he is טמא', words from the same פסוק
Forgetting that one is טמא
Forgetting that the place is the מקדש

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
"And it is hidden from him, and he is impure"
for forgetting the impurity, he is liable,
but he is not liable for forgetting the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the same ruling as step 6 but from a different phrase in the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability comes only for forgetting the טומאה, learned from 'ונעלם ממנו והוא טמא'. There is no liability for forgetting the מקדש.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: Liable for both kinds of forgetting
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל points out that 'ונעלם' is written twice, once for forgetting the טומאה and once for forgetting the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: 'And it is hidden' is written two times. This makes a person liable both for forgetting the טומאה and for forgetting the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל disagrees with the first two opinions and holds that a person is also liable for forgetting the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the word 'ונעלם' appears twice, each one teaches a separate case. One is forgetting the טומאה and the other is forgetting the מקדש. So for him, both kinds of forgetting bring a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Two times
To make someone liable

steps.whatToRemember: All three agree that forgetting the טומאה brings a קרבן. The argument is about forgetting the מקדש: רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא say no, and רבי ישמעאל says yes.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:
"And it is hidden", "and it is hidden", two times,
to make him liable for forgetting the impurity
and for forgetting the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with steps 6 and 7 by adding liability for forgetting the מקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The double 'ונעלם' makes a person liable both for forgetting the טומאה and for forgetting the מקדש.

steps.title: רב פפא: Shouldn't it be 'two that are six'?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי why the משנה counts 'two that are four', when there seem to be six: knowing at the beginning and at the end for the טומאה, for the קודש, and for the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: 'Two that are four'?! It should be 'two that are six'! There is knowing about the טומאה at the beginning and the end, knowing about the קודש at the beginning and the end, and knowing about the מקדש at the beginning and the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by challenging the count 'two that are four' at the opening of this פרק's משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening משנה says 'ידיעות הטומאה are two that are four'. רב פפא argues that the cases taught in this פרק add up to six: three subjects, and each one has knowing at the beginning and knowing at the end. So the number four looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Two that are four', the count at the start of the מסכת
States of knowing or awareness
At the beginning and at the end, before and after the forgetting
Sacrificial food that may be eaten

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
Two that are four?!
phrases.notes: He is quoting the opening line of this פרק's משנה: 'ידיעות הטומאה שתים שהן ארבע'.

phrases.english: They are two that are six:
awareness of the impurity at the beginning and at the end,
awareness of the sacrificial food at the beginning and at the end,
awareness of the Temple at the beginning and at the end!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: שְׁתַּיִם שֶׁהֵן אַרְבַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה has ended, and the גמרא opens by questioning the count at the start of the מסכת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opening משנה's wording 'שתים שהן ארבע'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There are three subjects, טומאה, קודש and מקדש, and each has knowing at the beginning and at the end. That makes six, not four.

steps.title: אביי pushes back: by your counting there would be eight
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers רב פפא's question with a counter-challenge. If you count every kind of knowing separately, there are eight, not six, because the טומאה for קודש and the טומאה for מקדש would each count separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, there are eight kinds of knowing! There is the טומאה connected to קודש and the טומאה connected to מקדש, each at the beginning and at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי does not answer directly. He turns רב פפא's own way of counting back on him and shows that it leads to eight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא counted six: beginning and end for טומאה, קודש, and מקדש. אביי says that the משנה mentions טומאה twice, once in the קודש case and once in the מקדש case. So if you split things up the way רב פפא did, you get eight. His point is that the count in the משנה should not be built by splitting everything apart.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: turning the questioner's own logic back on him
Eight
Cases or states (here, kinds of knowing)
Beginning and end: knowing before forgetting, and finding out afterward

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
phrases.notes: This is אביי answering רב פפא's question from the step before.

phrases.english: there are eight kinds of knowing,
for there is the impurity connected to sacred food
and the impurity connected to the Temple, at the beginning and at the end!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counter-challenge to רב פפא's question in Step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's way of counting six ידיעות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If every kind of knowing counts separately, the count becomes eight, so splitting things up that way cannot be what the משנה means.

steps.title: רב פפא rejects eight: impurity is one category, so six remains
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rejects אביי's push to eight. טומאה is one single category whether it is about קודש or מקדש, so his original question of six still stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is no problem, since it is one name of טומאה. In any case, there are six!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brushes off אביי's counter-challenge and insists that his question is still alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being טמא is the same fact in both cases. You knew you were טמא and then forgot it, whether you went on to eat קודש or enter the מקדש. So the two טומאה cases count as one. That brings us back to six: טומאה, קודש, and מקדש, each at the beginning and the end. The question is still why the משנה says only four.

keyTerms.meaning: That is not difficult: dismissing a challenge
One name of טומאה: the same category in both cases
In any case: the original problem remains
Six

phrases.english: That is not difficult,
it is all one name of impurity.
In any case there are six!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא, שֵׁם טוּמְאָה אַחַת הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's counter-challenge and brings back the question from Step 9
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the count should be eight
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: טומאה for קודש and טומאה for מקדש are one category and should not be counted twice.

steps.title: רב פפא's answer: there are eight, but only the four that lead to an offering count
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers his own question. There really are eight kinds of knowing. The four at the beginning do not on their own lead to a קרבן, so the תנא skips them. The four at the end do lead to a קרבן, so the תנא counts them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Really there are eight. The first four, which do not bring him to a קרבן, the תנא does not count. The last four, which do bring him to a קרבן, he does count.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא now agrees there are eight. He explains that the 'four' in the משנה means only the four kinds of knowing at the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing at the beginning is needed, but by itself it never makes a person bring a קרבן. Without finding out at the end, he would never know he sinned. Finding out at the end is what actually brings the קרבן, so the תנא counts those four. Counting טומאה separately for קודש and for מקדש, the four at the end are: טומאה for קודש, קודש, טומאה for מקדש, and מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually: introducing the true answer
The first ones (the knowing at the beginning)
The last ones (the knowing at the end)
To an offering: leading to the obligation to bring a קרבן
He counts it (the תנא includes it in his number)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two steps. In Step 11, רב פפא said the count was six. Here he agrees it is eight, counting טומאה once for קודש and once for מקדש. Then he explains why only four of the eight are counted.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לְעוֹלָם תַּמְנֵי הָוְיָין,
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Really there are eight,
the first four,
phrases.notes: The first four means the knowing at the beginning, before he forgot.

phrases.english: which do not bring him to an offering,
he does not count;
the last four,
which do bring him to an offering,
he does count.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לְעוֹלָם תַּמְנֵי הָוְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how many kinds of knowing there are, raised in Steps 9 to 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains which items the תנא chose to count
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'four' in the משנה seemed to leave out some kinds of knowing.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are eight, but the תנא counts only the four at the end, because those are the ones that lead to a קרבן.

steps.title: Second version: only the four found nowhere else in the Torah count
steps.stepSummary: Some report רב פפא's answer the opposite way. The four at the beginning are counted because nowhere else in the Torah is knowing at the beginning needed. The four at the end are found everywhere, so the תנא does not count them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רב פפא said: Really there are eight. The first four, which are not found anywhere in the whole Torah, the תנא counts. The last four, which are found throughout the whole Torah, he does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second report of רב פפא's answer. It agrees there are eight but flips which four the משנה counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For every other sin brought with a קרבן, you only need to find out afterward. Knowing at the beginning is a special rule found only here in טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. So this version says the משנה counts the new and unusual part, the four at the beginning. The usual part, the four at the end, goes without saying.

keyTerms.meaning: They are not found
They are found
In the entire Torah: in all other cases of קרבנות for sins

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree there are eight kinds of knowing and that the משנה counts four. The first version counts the four at the end, because they lead to the קרבן. The second version counts the four at the beginning, because that requirement is unique to this topic.
steps.whyThisMatters: Knowing at the beginning is a requirement unique to טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. That is the basic idea behind the whole משנה of 'ידיעות הטומאה שתים שהן ארבע'.

phrases.english: And there are those who say: Rav Pappa said:
Really there are eight;
and the first four,
which are not found in the whole Torah,
phrases.notes: Elsewhere a sin offering only needs you to find out afterward. Knowing beforehand is required only here.

phrases.english: he does count;
the last four,
which are found in the whole Torah,
he does not count.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לְעוֹלָם תַּמְנֵי הָוְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of רב פפא's answer from Step 12, with the reasoning flipped
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains which items the תנא chose to count (second version)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following Step 12, one might think the תנא counts the knowing at the end.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תנא counts the four at the beginning, because they are a new rule found only here. The four at the end are standard throughout the Torah.

steps.title: רב פפא asks about forgetting the laws of impurity
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks: if a person forgot the laws of טומאה themselves, does that count as the kind of 'forgetting' that makes him bring a קרבן?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: if the laws of טומאה were hidden from him, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא opens a new question. Until now the forgetting was about the facts, like not knowing he touched something impure. Now he asks what happens if the person forgot the law itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every case so far was about forgetting a fact: that he became impure, or that this was the מקדש. רב פפא asks whether forgetting a הלכה also counts as העלם טומאה. The גמרא will first need to figure out exactly what case he means.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question (raised a halachic doubt)
They were hidden from him (he forgot or did not know)
The laws of ritual impurity

phrases.english: Rav Pappa raised a question:
If the laws of impurity were hidden from him, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from counting the kinds of knowing to a new question about what counts as forgetting.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether forgetting a law of טומאה (rather than a fact) counts as העלם טומאה for a קרבן.

steps.title: What case could רב פפא mean? Not basic Torah laws
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case רב פפא means. It cannot mean someone who did not know whether a שרץ or a frog is impure, because any schoolchild knows that.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say he did not know whether a שרץ is impure or a frog is impure, that is something you learn in the schoolhouse!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is trying to pin down the exact case of רב פפא's question. It throws out the simplest option, and this sets up the real case in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether a שרץ or a frog is impure is written openly in the Torah. A child learning חומש knows it, so it can never really count as 'hidden'. So רב פפא must mean something more subtle.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? (what situation are we talking about)
A creeping creature whose dead body makes things impure
A frog
Go read it in the schoolhouse: something every child knows

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say that he did not know
whether a שרץ is impure
or whether a frog is impure,
that is a 'go read it in the schoolhouse' thing!
phrases.notes: He means it's written right in the חומש, so it can't count as truly unknown.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact case behind רב פפא's question and rules out the simplest version.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact situation רב פפא is asking about.

steps.title: The real case: touching a lentil-sized piece
steps.stepSummary: The case is someone who knows a שרץ makes impure, but touched a lentil-sized piece and did not know whether that small amount makes impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he knew about the טומאה of a שרץ. The case is where he touched a lentil-sized piece, and he did not know whether a lentil-size makes impure or does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real case of רב פפא's question. The person knows the general law, but not a smaller detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the case is truly in doubt. He knows the basic rule that a שרץ makes impure, but he does not know the size detail (a כעדשה). The question becomes whether partial knowledge like this counts as knowing or forgetting.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (introduces the true case)
The size of a lentil: the smallest amount of a שרץ that makes impure
Makes impure

phrases.english: Really, he knew about the impurity of a שרץ;
and the case is where he touched a lentil-sized piece,
and he did not know whether a lentil-size
makes impure or does not make impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers 'what is the case' with a subtler situation.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He knew the general טומאה of a שרץ but not that a lentil-size amount makes impure.

steps.title: The two sides: general knowing or detail forgotten?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא lays out both sides. Since he knows a שרץ makes impure, maybe this counts as knowing. Or since he did not know about the lentil-size, maybe it counts as forgetting.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law? Since he knows that a שרץ makes impure in general, is it 'knowing'? Or perhaps, since he did not know whether a lentil-size makes impure, is it 'forgetting'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא spells out the question itself, with the reasoning on each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: knowing the general rule is enough, so he is not someone who 'forgot'. Side two: what counts is the exact amount he touched, and about that he had no idea, so it is a real העלמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Knowing / awareness
Hiding: something being forgotten or unknown
Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)

phrases.english: What is the law?
Since he knows that a שרץ makes impure in general,
is it 'knowing'?
Or perhaps,
since about a lentil-size he did not know
whether it makes impure or does not make impure,
is it 'forgetting'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי? כֵּיוָן דְּיָדַע דִּמְטַמֵּא שֶׁרֶץ בָּעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two sides of רב פפא's question, now that the case is defined.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether general knowledge of a שרץ's טומאה counts as knowing, even though the lentil-size detail was unknown.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cannot settle רב פפא's question, so it is left standing: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends רב פפא's question without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means no proof was found either way. The question of whether knowing the general rule counts as 'knowing' stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's question, whether forgetting a detail like the lentil-size counts as העלם טומאה when you know the general rule, is left as a תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רב פפא's question without a ruling.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה asks about a newcomer who never knew where the מקדש was
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks about a man from בבל who came to ארץ ישראל and did not know where the מקדש was. Does he bring a קרבן?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: a man from בבל who went up to ארץ ישראל, and the place of the מקדש was hidden from him, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins, this time about the מקדש side of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This man never knew where the מקדש was, because he just arrived. The question is whether that counts as 'forgetting the מקדש' when he walks in while impure. It also asks whether his general knowledge that a מקדש exists counts as 'knowing at the beginning'.

keyTerms.meaning: A person from בבל (Babylonia)
Went up to ארץ ישראל
The location of the מקדש

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya raised a question:
A man from Bavel who went up to Eretz Yisrael,
and the place of the מקדש was hidden from him: what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question, now about not knowing the מקדש instead of not knowing the טומאה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a newcomer who never knew the מקדש's location is obligated in a קרבן for entering while impure.

steps.title: Whose opinion is this question based on?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי ירמיה's question. Under רבי עקיבא there is no קרבן for forgetting the מקדש at all. Under רבי ישמעאל, knowing at the beginning is not needed. So under neither view does the question seem to matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom? If according to רבי עקיבא, who requires knowing at the beginning, he does not obligate for forgetting the מקדש at all! If according to רבי ישמעאל, who does obligate for forgetting the מקדש, he does not require knowing at the beginning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי ירמיה's question by asking which תנא it could follow, and shows it seems pointless under both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question only matters if two things are both true: forgetting the מקדש brings a קרבן, and knowing at the beginning is required. רבי עקיבא holds the second but not the first. רבי ישמעאל holds the first but not the second, so nobody holds both.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? (which opinion is this based on)
Knowing at the beginning (before the forgetting)
Forgetting that this is the מקדש
Obligates (to bring a קרבן)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two תנאים: רבי עקיבא requires knowing at the beginning but gives no קרבן for forgetting the מקדש. רבי ישמעאל gives a קרבן for forgetting the מקדש but does not require knowing at the beginning.

phrases.english: According to whom?
If according to Rabbi Akiva,
who requires knowing at the beginning,

phrases.aramaic: הָא לָא מְחַיֵּיב עַל הֶעְלֵם מִקְדָּשׁ!
phrases.english: he does not obligate for forgetting the מקדש!
If according to Rabbi Yishmael,
who does obligate for forgetting the מקדש,
he does not require knowing at the beginning!
phrases.notes: So for רבי ישמעאל it makes no difference that the newcomer never knew where the מקדש was in the first place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רבי ירמיה's question has any relevance.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה's question about the newcomer from בבל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The question needs both a קרבן for העלם מקדש and a requirement of knowing at the beginning. רבי עקיבא holds only the second and רבי ישמעאל holds only the first, so the question seems to fit neither.

steps.title: The question only matters according to רבי
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה's question is needed only according to רבי. רבי requires knowing at the beginning, is מחייב for forgetting the מקדש, and counts knowledge from a teacher's house as knowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the question is needed only according to רבי. He requires knowing at the beginning, holds a person liable for forgetting the מקדש, and says that knowledge learned in one's teacher's house counts as knowing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 20. It finds one opinion where רבי ירמיה's question really does matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge said neither רבי עקיבא nor רבי ישמעאל fits the question. רבי holds the parts of both views that make the question work: liability for forgetting the מקדש, and a need for knowing at the beginning. He also counts what you learned from your teacher as knowing. So the man from בבל, who learned that there is a מקדש, may count as having known.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for... (the case or view where the question applies)
Knowing at the beginning, before the forgetting
Forgetting that a place is the מקדש
Knowledge a person learned in his teacher's study hall

phrases.english: No, it is needed only
according to רבי,
who requires knowing at the beginning,
and holds one liable for forgetting the מקדש,
and says that knowledge from his teacher's house
phrases.notes: This goes back to earlier in the מסכת (דף ה). Learning the law from your rebbe counts as the first knowing.

phrases.english: is called knowing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 20 by naming a view where the question applies.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the question to a specific opinion (רבי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No view makes רבי ירמיה's question relevant.
steps.terutzMaskana: Under רבי, who requires first knowing, is מחייב for forgetting the מקדש, and counts a teacher's lesson as knowing, the question is real.

steps.title: Does knowing a מקדש exists count as knowing?
steps.stepSummary: Under רבי, the גמרא lays out both sides. Knowing that a מקדש exists might be enough knowing, or not knowing its location might count as forgetting.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law? Since he knows there is a מקדש in the world, maybe that counts as knowing. Or perhaps, since he does not know where it is, it counts as forgetting.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the question has a home in רבי's view, the גמרא spells out the two possible sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man knows the general fact that a מקדש exists. He is missing the specific detail of where it is. The question is whether general knowledge is enough to count as the first knowing.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the law?
In the world (somewhere)
Its location
Being hidden from him, which counts as forgetting

phrases.english: What is the law?
Since he knows
that there is a מקדש in the world,
it is knowing;
or perhaps,
since he does not know its location,
it is hidden from him?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי? כֵּיוָן דְּיָדַע דְּאִיכָּא מִקְדָּשׁ בָּעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two sides of the question that step 21 showed is valid.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does general knowledge that a מקדש exists count as the first knowing, when the location is unknown?

steps.title: The question is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cannot decide רבי ירמיה's question, so it stays standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this question without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither side is proven. This matches the earlier lentil-sized שרץ question, which also ended unresolved. In both cases the issue is partial knowledge.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question is unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: Both רב פפא's question and רבי ירמיה's question ask whether partial knowledge counts as knowing. Both are left as תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question raised in step 22 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The case of knowing a מקדש exists but not its location remains undecided.

steps.title: Source for treating the added עזרה like the original
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that entering the added part of the עזרה is the same as entering the original part, and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: the same applies to one who enters the עזרה, and so on. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. It is setting up a search for the source behind that line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the added parts of the עזרה have the same holiness as the original. It also says such additions need a king, a נביא, the אורים ותומים, and the סנהדרין. The גמרא wants to know where this comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: The courtyard of the מקדש
From where do we know these things?

phrases.english: The same applies to one who enters the courtyard, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' stands for the rest of the משנה. The added parts of the courtyard count like the original, and additions need a king, a נביא, the אורים ותומים and the סנהדרין.

phrases.english: From where are these matters known?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה after the תיקו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the added עזרה having the full holiness, and for how additions are made.

steps.title: רב שימי בר חייא begins quoting a פסוק about the משכן
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר חייא answers with the פסוק about building everything exactly like the pattern shown to משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר חייא said: because the פסוק says, 'According to all that I show you, the form of the משכן and the form of all its vessels...'
steps.whatsHappening: An answer begins. רב שימי בר חייא brings a פסוק, and the quote continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק stresses copying the exact pattern of the משכן. The full lesson from it comes after the quote is finished. For now we only have the start of the source.

keyTerms.meaning: Form, pattern
The Tabernacle in the desert
Its vessels

phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ḥiyya said:
As the verse states:
"According to all that I show you,
the form of the Tabernacle
and the form of all its vessels

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שִׁימִי בַּר חִיָּיא, דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the source question from step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the פסוק in שמות about following the pattern of the משכן and its vessels. The quote continues beyond this point.
